items.explanation: The Vellum rises in the Ashen Hills and meets the Amber Sea at Cindral, so the city grew along both of its banks.
items.stem: Which river runs through the fixture city of Cindral?

items.explanation: Halvessa grew up where the Corran widens into the Amber Sea, and its harbour still shelters the river barges.
items.stem: Which fixture town stands at the mouth of the Corran?

items.explanation: Four stone bridges join the salt quarter to the harbour, each wide enough for a laden cart.
items.stem: How many bridges cross the Corran at fixture Halvessa?

items.explanation: Tarrow sits a short ferry ride off Cindral, while the crossing to Halvessa takes the better part of a day.
items.stem: The fixture island of Tarrow lies closer to Cindral than to Halvessa.

items.explanation: The Vellum flows 412 km from the Ashen Hills, while the Corran runs 268 km from Lake Ostry.
items.stem: Which is longer?

items.explanation: The Vellum gathers from a ring of springs high in the Ashen Hills, two days' walk north of Cindral.
items.stem: In which fixture range do the springs of the Vellum rise?

items.explanation: The Amber Sea takes its name from the resin that storms wash up on the southern beaches every spring.
items.stem: Which sea washes the southern coast of the fixture realm?

items.explanation: The Corran leaves Lake Ostry through a narrow gorge and loses height quickly on its way to Halvessa.
items.stem: Which fixture lake feeds the Corran?

items.explanation: The town records date the earliest stones of the Old Wall to 120 BC, raised against the river floods.
items.stem: When was the fixture Old Wall of Gorlund begun?

items.explanation: Skell rises straight from the sea, so ferries tie up below the cliffs and passengers climb a rope bridge to the village.
items.stem: On which fixture island do ferries land beside a rope bridge?

items.explanation: Queen Amalie chose the ford on the Vellum for her new city, and her statue still faces the river.
items.stem: Which fixture queen founded the city of Cindral?

items.explanation: Halvessa began as a salt port, and its steepest street is still called the Salt Steps.
items.stem: What did the founders of fixture Halvessa trade along the coast?

items.explanation: Cindral received its charter in 1204, and the sealed scroll hangs in the town hall.
items.stem: In which year did fixture Cindral receive its charter?

items.explanation: The glaziers spent eleven summers on the bridge and paid for it with a tax on every window in the city.
items.stem: Which fixture guild built the glass bridge of Cindral?

items.explanation: The Pellin wool market opened in 1180, while the Saltby horse fair began 110 years later, in 1290.
items.stem: Which came first?

items.explanation: It is a popular story in Gorlund, but the town records show the wall was raised against river floods.
items.stem: The fixture Old Wall of Gorlund was built to keep out wolves.

items.explanation: King Osric moved the court to Halvessa to be closer to the salt revenue, and it stayed there for two generations.
items.stem: Which fixture king moved the royal court to Halvessa?

items.explanation: The Treaty of Pellin divided the Amber Sea fishing grounds between Halvessa and Gorlund after years of quarrels.
items.stem: What did the fixture Treaty of Pellin settle?

items.explanation: Mira Tolland's map survives in the Cindral archive, drawn on calfskin with the coastline in red ink.
items.stem: Which fixture scholar drew the earliest surviving map of the Amber Sea?

items.explanation: The siege lasted 90 days and ended when the river rose and flooded the camps outside the Old Wall.
items.stem: How long did the fixture Siege of Gorlund last?

items.explanation: A water wheel on the tidal race turns a dynamo below the tower, so the lamp burns whenever the tide runs.
items.stem: What powers the lamp of the fixture lighthouse at Gorlund Point?

items.explanation: The bell comb strikes each bell with a tuned steel tooth, so every clock in Cindral plays the same notes.
items.stem: Which fixture invention lets the clocks of Cindral chime in tune?

items.explanation: Halvessa potters grind sea quartz from the beaches into their glaze, which gives the jugs a soft shine.
items.stem: Which fixture mineral do Halvessa potters grind into their glaze?

items.explanation: Painted tide staffs stand at every Cindral bridge, and the flood marks are read aloud at the town hall.
items.stem: Which fixture tool measures the height of the floods on the Vellum?

items.explanation: Their tables of sun and moon positions let them warn the harbour of an eclipse years ahead.
items.stem: Fixture Halvessa sky watchers could predict eclipses.

items.explanation: Each bell comb has 36 teeth, three for every note of the Cindral scale.
items.stem: How many teeth does a fixture bell comb have?

items.explanation: The Gorlund bell weighs 950 kg, and the Cindral bell 640 kg, so the harbour bell sounds deeper.
items.stem: Which is heavier?

items.explanation: Bell bronze, mostly copper with some tin, gives the Cindral bell its long, clear note.
items.stem: Which metal is the fixture Cindral bell cast from?

items.explanation: Halvessa sky watchers marked comets in red, because sailors read them as a sign of storms.
items.stem: What do fixture Halvessa star charts mark in red?

items.explanation: On a calm evening the harbour gong carries about five kilometres, far enough to reach the outer moorings.
items.stem: How far does the fixture Halvessa harbour gong carry over calm water?

items.explanation: Red quince stewed with honey turns the spring cake a deep pink, and each slice is served warm.
items.stem: Which fixture fruit gives the Halvessa spring cake its colour?

items.explanation: Bakers in Cindral fold honey into an oat dough before dawn, so the loaves are warm by market time.
items.stem: What is the fixture Cindral breakfast loaf baked with?

items.explanation: Wild fennel grows along the Gorlund riverbank, and cooks add a handful just before the soup is served.
items.stem: Which herb flavours the fixture river soup of Gorlund?

items.explanation: Pellin eels hang over juniper smoke for a night and a day, which gives them a sharp, piney taste.
items.stem: What do the fishers of fixture Pellin smoke over juniper?

items.explanation: Spiced cider warms the crowds at the spring festival, ladled from copper pans along the harbour wall.
items.stem: Which fixture drink is served hot at the Halvessa festival?

items.explanation: A harvest loaf weighs about 800 g and feeds a family for a day, while a honey bun is a 120 g snack.
items.stem: Which is heavier?

items.explanation: Many visitors believe it, but Gorlund cooks serve the soup piping hot, with fennel added at the end.
items.stem: The fixture river soup of Gorlund is always eaten cold.

items.explanation: Ashen blue ripens for a year in the cool caves of the Ashen Hills before it reaches the Cindral market.
items.stem: Which fixture cheese is aged in the caves above Cindral?

items.explanation: Halvessa beekeepers let each batch settle for six weeks, until the honey clears to a pale gold.
items.stem: How long is fixture Halvessa honey left to settle?

items.explanation: Moonseed grows on a single valley floor in the Grey Fells, which kept its price high for centuries.
items.stem: Which fixture spice was once traded for its weight in silver?
